.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r12/task/solution/solve.sh, solution/app/package.json, solution/app/src/runtime.ts and src/custom-editor.js (targeted greps only, not a full read)
evidence:
REACHABILITY (no unreachable item found). Every capability is reachable from the pinned runtime plus the public network: Node 22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 are installed globally with NODE_PATH in both environment/Dockerfile:3,9-12 and tests/Dockerfile:9,16-22; network_mode is public (task.toml:22,38), so a parser/formatter can be vendored into /app and a browser can be installed for self-testing; the agent Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template. Launch facts the verifier relies on (tests/test.sh:97-111: node server.js, uid 65534, env -i, DB_PATH, cwd outside /app, writable copy) are all stated in integration.md:3,9. instruction.md:3 says 'six notes' and six exist. The hard runtime asks (five-second budget on endless loops, last-good picture with typed values and canvas, preview fetch rejection, dynamic-code refusal, line numbers for rejections) are demonstrably reachable: the golden does them with acorn instrumentation, a sandbox='allow-scripts' iframe and a CSP with connect-src 'none' (solution/app/src/runtime.ts:1,7,33-63,223-229,378), and scripted golden results on these bytes show all 3 gate, 42 functional-suite and polish checks true (results/editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json; artifact hashes in raw-evidence-index.json re-computed and all 16 match). No configured judge run exists for these bytes, so judge-side behaviour below is NOT EXERCISED.

AMBIGUITY 1 (graded, credible second reading). ui.md:9: 'A continuous multi-caret typing burst is one Undo action; Redo restores it.' Nothing says what ends a 'continuous burst'. Reading A (golden): a burst continues until the caret set moves or another kind of edit happens, however long the pauses are (custom-editor.js:574-583 groups by caret key, no clock). Reading B: a burst is typing that is continuous in time, and a pause starts a new Undo group; this is the mainstream convention ('burst' itself connotes rapid keys; CodeMirror groups history by an idle delay of roughly half a second to a second). The criterion cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (functional/judge.toml:101, weight 2.0) says only 'Type the five characters MULTI as normal sequential keys ... One Undo must remove all fifteen inserted characters ... Fails if ... the burst needs more than one Undo', with no instruction about timing. The scripted golden check used page.keyboard.type('MULTI') (editor.cjs:149), i.e. keys milliseconds apart, so it says nothing about a judge that presses five keys in five tool calls seconds apart.

AMBIGUITY 2 (graded, credible second reading). ui.md:5: 'Show numbered logical lines and the current line and column.' The base of the column is not stated, while behaviour.md:3 does take care to say 'one-based line number' for errors. Reading A (golden): one-based column, 'Ln 1, Col 10' at the end of a nine-character line (editor.cjs:39-43,187). Reading B: column as the count of characters left of the caret (zero-based, as Emacs shows it). cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers (judge.toml:38, weight 1.0) fails 'if the readout disagrees with the caret position' and cw_undo_restores_caret (judge.toml:128, weight 1.5) requires 'the line and column readout must show that position', and neither states a base, so the verdict for a zero-based app rests on the judge's private assumption. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:15 names 'coordinate bases' explicitly as something to check against public instructions. The same sentence is also silent on whether a column counts graphemes or UTF-16 units after an emoji; no criterion reads the readout on such a line, so that part is ungraded.

UNGRADED AMBIGUITIES (reported as required; none changes a criterion verdict as written). (a) behaviour.md:3 'The browser may execute supported code in the preview' - 'supported code' is undefined; presumably it permits running an instrumented copy while the editor keeps the exact source. (b) behaviour.md:5 'If a later run throws, is stopped or exceeds the five-second run budget ... restore that picture' does not say whether an unhandled Promise rejection, or one failing inline script in an HTML file, counts as a run that 'throws'; cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line and cw_error_message_and_line only read the console. (c) behaviour.md:5 'pending timer or Promise callbacks until that run settles': a legitimate endless setInterval or requestAnimationFrame animation is by this text ended after five seconds; requestAnimationFrame is not named either way. (d) behaviour.md:3 asks for a one-based line number for 'a Promise rejection that nothing handles' and says the message may be the text of a non-Error 'rejected value'; a rejected plain value carries no stack, so its line is only obtainable by instrumenting or wrapping Promise (the golden does); the criterion uses Error objects only. (e) security.md:3 'must not be able to reach the network from the preview' is narrowed by its own colon to fetch; images, stylesheets and self-navigation of the frame are neither clearly in nor out, and only fetch is graded. (f) ui.md:17 'whether the draft differs from what is saved' does not say whether an edited title or filename, or a never-saved New draft, counts as differing; cw_unsaved_marker edits source only. (g) ui.md:17 'After ... a replacement ... put keyboard focus back in the code so typing continues at the caret' combined with ui.md:11 'Replace current ... then moves to the match that follows it' (which is selected in the editor) means a key typed straight after Replace current overwrites the next match; coherent but surprising, and the polish criterion checks only Replace all. (h) overview.md:3 does not say what happens for a filename that ends in neither .js nor .html. (i) cw_basic_run_output and cw_run_starts_fresh_document write to the preview page body; the brief does not say the .js source runs after a body exists, though any sensible preview document provides one.

What is done well: the runtime contract is fully stated and matches test.sh; policy.md:3,5 explicitly frees layout, labels, routes, schema and error wording; the single-caret undo granularity is explicitly left open (ui.md:9) and the criteria respect it; the restore-retry requirement admits idempotency-key, base-revision and content-dedupe designs and the criterion passes all three; the criteria accept ten seconds where the brief says about five.
counterexample: 1) Conforming alternative that can fail: an app whose Undo history, like CodeMirror, closes a typing group after about 750 ms without a key. For a person, typing MULTI at three carets is one Undo, satisfying ui.md:9. The judge presses M, U, L, T, I through five separate browser key-press tool calls several seconds apart; the app records five groups, one Undo removes only the three 'I' characters, and cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (weight 2.0) fails on 'the burst needs more than one Undo'. The same app passes if the judge happens to send the five keys in one Playwright keyboard.type call, so the verdict depends on the judge's tool choice, not on the product. 2) Conforming alternative that can fail: an app showing 'Ln 2, Col 5' when five characters precede the caret (zero-based column). A judge that assumes one-based columns fails cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers and cw_undo_restores_caret (combined weight 2.5) for 'readout disagrees with the caret position'; a judge that assumes zero-based would equally fail the golden's 'Col 6'. Neither outcome is derivable from the public notes.
suggested_fix: In ui.md say that the multi-caret burst stays one Undo action across pauses and ends only when the carets are moved or another kind of action is taken (or, alternatively, tell the judge in cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic to send the five keys in one uninterrupted keyboard action); and either state in ui.md that line and column are one-based, or add to both readout criteria that a consistently zero-based or one-based column is accepted. Optionally tidy the ungraded items: define 'supported code', and say whether an unhandled rejection restores the last-good picture.
